patch_description:
The current program achieves a combined score of 0.60 with worst_group_margin_mean of 0.32, which indicates that the hardest samples are not being separated robustly enough. The recommendation from prior experiments suggests adding a global mirror-pair ZZ entangler layer.

The key insight is that mirror-pair correlations (0↔7, 1↔6, 2↔5, 3↔4) can capture long-range symmetries that improve separation on difficult samples. By introducing a ZZ layer with a single shared parameter across mirror pairs, we maintain parameter economy (staying at ~9 params) while tightening worst-group margins without overfitting.

Current structure has 7 distinct parameters. Adding one shared "zz_global" parameter across 4 mirror-pair ZZ gates gives us 8 distinct parameters (9 total with readout params), which is acceptable and aligns with the recommendation that parameter economy always scores higher with no diminishing returns.

This targeted enhancement directly addresses the identified weakness: worst_group_margin_mean is the lowest metric (0.32 vs validation_margin_mean of 0.64), so improving worst-case separation should boost the combined score.
